verdict.summary: Vicor offers one of the batch's cleanest balance sheets and one of its least forgiving valuations. Q2 2026 revenue was $143.35 million, up 49.3% year over year and 26.9% sequentially; GAAP gross margin was 58.0%, GAAP net income $49.8 million and diluted EPS $1.04. Advanced Products including royalty revenue rose 55.5% to $94.2 million, while backlog increased sequentially to $379.7 million. The AI transmission is power density: accelerator racks require efficient conversion close to the processor, and higher-power architectures can increase dollars of advanced power modules per rack. Royalties add attractive economics, but they also complicate comparisons because a new license agreement boosted the quarter and a prior-year patent settlement affected the base. Cash of $453.6 million against $7.6 million debt is exceptional. Both Common and Class B shares produce a $9.18 billion equity value at the recorded quote, not the public-class-only $6.85 billion figure. Wait: VICR has no executable trigger in the frozen bundle. business.overview:
Vicor sells high-density power-conversion modules in two product families, Brick Products and Advanced Products, and also earns royalty revenue from intellectual property. Revenue depends on design wins, production ramps, product mix and license economics rather than semiconductor units alone.

The AI transmission channel is rack power density. GPUs and custom accelerators require efficient conversion from rack-level distribution to low-voltage, high-current loads near the processor; Vicor's factorized power and vertical-delivery architectures target lower losses and smaller board area in those systems.

The model breaks if customers choose competing voltage-regulator architectures, design wins do not reach volume, manufacturing cannot scale, or royalty contributions prove episodic. Patent litigation, customer concentration and the rebuilt 76.0x EV/EBITDA multiple amplify any delay. Backlog rose to $379.7M, but customer acceptance, royalty accounting and the timing of high-density module ramps can make quarterly revenue uneven. The thesis fails if hyperscalers redesign power architectures, internalize conversion, or new capacity runs below the volume needed to support current margins.
business.moat: Vicor's moat is patented power-conversion architecture, high-frequency magnetics and packaging that deliver density close to the load. The economic proof is the 58.0% Q2 gross margin and royalty contribution, but the moat remains design-win dependent and must compete against integrated and multiphase alternatives.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: The July 22 Form 10-Q cover reports 34,389,014 Common shares plus 11,717,718 Class B shares, or 46,106,732 economically outstanding basic shares. Q2 EPS reconciles 45.936M basic weighted-average shares to 47.708M diluted through 1.772M options; 47.708M is the minimum observable diluted denominator, while a current point-in-time fully diluted total remains unavailable. At $199.1699, both classes imply $9.18B equity value; $453.6M cash and $7.6M debt produce about $8.74B EV. The board authorized a $150M repurchase program in addition to roughly $64.3M remaining, but authorization is capacity, not completed buying.

filings.finding: The Q2 Form 10-Q supports $143.35M revenue, 58.0% GAAP gross margin, $379.74M backlog and $453.58M cash; it also identifies the new royalty agreement and prior-year $45M patent-settlement comparability issue.

The August 27 Form 8-K supports a new $150M common-stock repurchase authorization; authorization creates purchase capacity but does not prove that Vicor acquired shares or establish any equity issuance.
The FY2025 Form 10-K supplies the product, patent, customer, manufacturing and design-win risk baseline needed to assess whether Q2 royalty and backlog growth represent durable operating economics.
